questions: Do line_loss_events drop to 0 on the sharpest bend with the wider span? If not, what is the next limit?
Does the robot still leave the track, and at what progress and at which bend type?
Is steering_oscillation higher or lower than the baseline at this lead of 4 cm and mass of 0.6 kg?
Does completion_time stay under 3.0 s with the lighter mass and narrower track, or is it limited by the drive?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If line losses are gone but the robot still goes off track, tell me whether a shorter lead (about 0.03 m) or a larger sensor pitch would help more. If completion is near 3.0 s, I will consider a larger wheel_radius.

intent: Test whether a wider five-sensor span (±3 cm) at a shorter 4 cm lead, with a lighter, slightly narrower chassis, stops the line losses and off-track exits that ended all 60 baseline runs. Expect line_loss_events near 0, progress well above the 0.10-0.15 baseline, and a first chance at completion on the oval and s-bend tracks.
learning: Baseline (no finishes, all off_track): progress 0.10-0.15, max_error about 0.061-0.065 m (close to the 0.0625 m limit), line_loss 1-2, steering_oscillation 0.07-0.15. Hypotheses for this iteration: (1) the 4 cm span is too narrow, so widening it to 6 cm reduces line losses; (2) the 5 cm lead reads the line too late, so 4 cm improves tracking; (3) a lighter 0.6 kg, 0.11 m track chassis gives faster response and speed closer to the 1.5 m/s needed. Measurements to check next: completion, progress, completion_time, line_loss_events, max_error and rms_error on every development track.
rationale: The only race evidence is the baseline (entityR2A, 60 trials, no finishes). Every run ended off track at about 10-15% progress. Max error was 0.061-0.065 m, essentially the 0.0625 m off-track limit, and line_loss_events was 1-2 per run. The robot is losing the line on bends and drifting out before the controller can recover. Two geometry causes fit this. First, the 4 cm array is too narrow: the line leaves the sensors on sharper bends, which matches the line losses and the off-track ends. Second, the 5 cm forward offset may read the line too late to correct the bend. Oscillation is low (0.07-0.15), so jitter is not the main failure. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit within range, since max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06 for any body width up to 0.19 m, so I will leave body_width alone. Changes: widen the array to x = -0.03 to +0.03 at 1.5 cm pitch, which keeps the tape under at least one sensor through sharp bends. Move the sensors to y = 0.04 m, a moderate lead that is shorter than the baseline and within the Integrator's suggested range. Reduce mass to 0.6 kg and wheel_track to 0.11 m to help the robot reach about 1.5 m/s and turn more readily. Keep sensor_size at 0.012 and wheel_radius at 0.03. Expected result: line_loss_events falls toward 0 and progress rises well above 0.15, with completion possible on the tightest bend. If the robot still goes off track with few line losses, the cause is more likely the forward offset or the gains.
